主题

叛乱分子遣返办公室发布的通告。

The following is a notification issued
by the officials of the office for the
repatriation of rebels:-
Sometime ago we obtained permission from the
Military Governor to establish an office for the
repatriation of rebels and to cooperate with the
leaders of the various revolutionary parties
and the prominent gentry and merchants of Shanghai.
In the office there was a Board of investigation
and the investigating officers were all rebels
leaders. The regulations of the office and the
general circumstances regarding its establishment
were published in the newspapers. Now the work
is nearly completed and the cause of the
establishment of the office and what it has done
are hereby published for the information of the
public.
Since 1913 the rebels of the various provinces
have stayed in Shanghai. The rebel leaders who
were dissatisfied with the system of government
established offices and raised disbanded soldiers
in order to be ready to start a revolution.
Therefore discharged military officers, disbanded
soldiers and rebels of the various provinces came
to Shanghai. A great number of these men joined
the rebel parties. When the revolution broke out
in the southwest of China last year, many of the
rebels in Shanghai joined the Republican armies
in the various provinces and thus the number of
rebels in Shanghai was greatly reduced. Now the
President has assumed office and the old constitution
has been restored. Dr. Sun Yat Sen has disbanded
the men who were under the command of Chen Chi
Mei and Mr. Huang Hsin has declared that he had
disposed of his men by paying them money from his
private purse, without getting a single cash from
the Government. Thus one can imagine the number
of rebels who are still in Shanghai. Later certain
rebel leaders went to Peking and applied for money
to send away the rebels from Shanghai. The Cabinet
despatched a telegram to the Shanghai Military
Governor, saying that if the amount of money
required for this purpose was not large, the
application might be approved. The Governor then
sent officers to approach the rebel leaders who
informed them that the rebels in Shanghai were
homeless and should be sent away. This information
was brought to the notice of the Cabinet. The
Cabinet in a reply granted the application but
as it had no money it requested Tuchun Feng to
raise the money. We then held many meetings with
the rebel leaders and the merchants and discussed
the ways in which rebels were to be repatriated.
We went to Nanking and asked Tuchun Feng to issue
$100,000 to be distributed among the rebels and
we also told the rebel leaders of the amount
asked for. Later we found difficulties in dealing
with the repatriation. Should we examine the
rebels one by one, they would think we were too
strict and did not treat them properly. If we
gave them money without investigation, we feared
that false representations would take place.
Moreover, we were not acquainted with the affairs
of the rebel parties, so it would be very hard
for us to make investigations. We therefore
gathered the rebel leaders, the gentry and
merchants together and discussed the matter.
The rebel leaders agreed to form a Board of
investigation. It was decided that after investigation
was over, the money should be paid to the

以下是叛乱分子遣返办公室官员发布的通告：
前此，我们已获得督军许可，设立叛乱分子遣返办公室，并与各革命党领袖及上海绅商合作。办公室内设调查委员会，调查员均由叛乱分子领袖担任。办公室章程及设立概况已登报公布。现工作已近尾声，特此公布设立该办公室之缘由及其所作所为，以告公众。
自1913年以来，各省叛乱分子滞留上海。那些对既定政府体制不满的叛乱分子领袖设立机构，招募散兵游勇，以备发动革命。因此，各省退伍军官、散兵及叛乱分子纷纷来到上海。这些人中大量加入了叛乱党派。去年中国西南爆发革命时，上海的许多叛乱分子加入了各省的共和军，致使上海叛乱分子人数大减。如今总统已就职，旧宪法已恢复。孙中山先生已解散陈其美麾下人员，黄兴先生亦声明已自掏腰包遣散其部属，未向政府索取分文。由此可以想见仍滞留上海的叛乱分子数量。后来，某些叛乱分子领袖前往北京，申请经费以遣送在上海的叛乱分子离沪。内阁致电上海督军，称若所需金额不大，可予批准。督军遂派员接触叛乱分子领袖，后者告知他们，在沪叛乱分子无家可归，应予遣送。此情况已呈报内阁知悉。内阁复函批准申请，但因无款可拨，请求督军冯国璋筹款。我们随后与叛乱分子领袖及绅商多次开会，商讨遣返叛乱分子之办法。我们前往南京，请督军冯国璋拨款10万元，分发给叛乱分子，并将所请金额告知叛乱分子领袖。后来我们在处理遣返事宜时发现困难。若逐一审查叛乱分子，他们会认为我们过于严苛，对待不当。若不查即发钱，又恐出现虚假冒领。此外，我们不熟悉各叛乱党派内部事务，故调查甚难。因此，我们将叛乱分子领袖、绅商召集在一起商议此事。叛乱分子领袖同意成立调查委员会。决定调查结束后，款项将支付给

representatives of each of the revolutionary
parties who forwarded the lists of names of
their men to be distributed and who should
undertake the responsibility of sending them
away. It was also decided that if the amount
of money issued by the Government did not
correspond with that which they required, it
would be divided proportionately. We decided
to send away the rebels who were in Shanghai
before July or August and who were unable to
return home, so we inserted a notice in the
newspaper that applications would be received
between the 13th and 17th September, both days
inclusive, but unexpectedly we received more
than 600 lists of names within 5 days, covering
over 28,000 men. Among these names many were
false which were forwarded with a view to
fraudulently obtaining money. The officer in
charge of the office handed the lists to the
Board of investigation. Mr. Tang Zah Bing
sent Messrs Jeu and Lan to investigate
the lists of names of men who are natives of
Hunan. The Board of investigation divided the
applicants into two classes. The 1st class
applicants are those who were passed as genuine
rebels and about $217,000 was required to
dispose of them, while the 2nd class applicants
are those who are not well known and no enquiries
can be made about them. These men number about
7,000. As the investigating officers do not
know them it is impossible for the officials to
know them because the officials are not acquainted
with the rebel parties. According to reasons,
these applications should be considered invalid,
but though they are not all proper, there must
be genuine rebels amongst them. Therefore these
men will also be paid and about $18,000 is
required to pay them. The rebel leaders have
sent in accounts of money which they lost in
the public cause and the total amount of these
is $228,000. Thus the three sums when added
together will amount to $463,000. This amount
is far different from that which the Government
has granted, i.e. $100,000. We then asked the
Military Governor to report the matter to the
Cabinet and Tuohun Feng, asking for instructions.
The investigating officers also telegraphed to
Peking asking for an increase. Later we received
a telegram from the Cabinet, stating that the
Government was in financial difficulties and
unable to raise such a large amount. But on
two occasions, the Government granted an increase
of $70,000, thus making a total of $170,000.
This still makes a great deficiency in the amount
the rebels require. If the amount of money granted
by the Government is distributed proportionately
amongst the rebels including the money lost in
the public cause, each rebel will receive a very
small sum which will do them no good. The
The Government and the Tuohun are unable
to raise any more, while the rebels wrote to us
asking for the issue of the money immediately as
the weather was getting cold. We then approached
the rebel leaders and told them that the money
they lost in the public cause could not be paid
as the amount of money granted by the Government
was not sufficient but would be paid to the
rebel applicants. We have now obtained permission

各革命党派的代表，由他们提交需分发款项的人员名单，并承担将其遣送的责任。还决定，若政府发放的金额与他们所需不符，将按比例分配。我们决定遣送那些在七月或八月之前就在上海且无法返乡的叛乱分子，因此在报纸上刊登通告，称将于9月13日至17日（含首尾两日）受理申请，但出乎意料的是，5天内收到600多份名单，涉及28,000余人。其中许多名字是假的，意在诈骗钱财。办公室负责人将名单移交调查委员会。唐赞冰（Tang Zah Bing，音译）先生派遣Jeu（音译）和Lan（音译）两位先生调查湖南籍人员名单。调查委员会将申请人分为两类。第一类申请人是被确认为真实叛乱分子者，遣散他们约需217,000元；第二类申请人是不为人知、无法查证者。这类人约有7,000名。由于调查员不认识他们，官员们也无法知晓，因为官员不熟悉叛乱党派。按理，这些申请应视为无效，但虽不尽合规，其中必有真正的叛乱分子。因此，这些人也将获得付款，约需18,000元。叛乱分子领袖提交了他们在公共事业中损失的账目，总额为228,000元。这三笔款项相加，总计463,000元。此数额与政府批准的100,000元相差甚远。我们随即请督军将此事项上报内阁及督军冯国璋（Tuohun Feng，原文拼写有误，指冯国璋），请示指示。调查员也致电北京，要求增加拨款。后来我们收到内阁电报，称政府财政困难，无法筹集如此巨款。但政府两次批准增加70,000元，使总额达到170,000元。这与叛乱分子所需金额仍有巨大缺口。若将政府批准的金额（包括公共事业损失费）按比例分发给叛乱分子，每人所得极少，无济于事。政府和冯督军（Tuohun）无法再筹措更多款项，而叛乱分子致信我们，因天气渐冷，要求立即发款。我们随后接触叛乱分子领袖，告知他们，因政府拨款不足，其在公共事业中的损失无法支付，但会支付给叛乱分子申请人。我们现在已获得

from the Military Governor to distribute the
$170,000. The 2nd class applicants will
divide $18,000 and the balance $152,000 will
be paid to the 1st class applicants, including
the Hunanese rebels. The total amount to be
paid is about $172,300. The rebel leaders
after getting the money are requested to pay
their men as soon after as possible and tell
them to return home. They shall not stay in
Shanghai any longer or make trouble. This
is what the Government pays them for. The
date and the regulations governing the issue
of the repatriation funds are published as
under and the office for the repatriation of
rebels is abolished.

REGULATIONS governing the issue of
repatriation funds:-

1. Time. On Oct. 21st, 22nd, and 23rd
From 8 a.m. to 12 noon and
" 1 p.m. " 5 p.m.
(200 lists of names will receive
payment each day).

2. Place. The Military Officers Association
next door to the Chu Tseng Yin Miao
in the Nyi Kai Lee alleyway
at Kau Chong Liao.

3. Applicants should bring with them their
seal, those who reported their names
individually to the office should furnish
a duplicate of their original report as
to their names, native place and career.
Those who report their names through their
leaders should bring with them a duplicate
of the report furnished by their leaders.
4. Those who reported their names
individually should claim payment themselves
while those who reported their names through
their leaders, should be paid through their
leaders. In the latter case they should claim
payment from their leaders.
5. Claimants should travel by the following
route viz Zia Jao Road, pass Hwui-ning Guild,
to Nyi Kai Lee, then enter the Chu Tseng Yin
Miao, where they will be examined as to their
names and required to fill in a receipt form.
With this receipt they go to the Military
Officers Association Building next door,
where they will be paid on presenting the
receipt. The blank receipts have been
made ready for use by the Office.
6. The payment will be supervised by deputies
of General Feng, Governor Yang, the Investigation
Committee, the local gentry, civil, military,
and police authorities together with the
gentry and merchants.
7. Claimants should adhere to the regulations and
time and they will get the money without fail.
8. The Military Officers Association Building
will be used for the payment of repatriation
money. The office will be abolished as soon
as the money is paid.

督军许可，分发这170,000元。第二类申请人将分得18,000元，余下的152,000元将支付给第一类申请人，包括湖南籍叛乱分子。支付总额约为172,300元。叛乱分子领袖领到款项后，须尽快发给其部属，并令其返乡。不得再滞留上海或滋事。这正是政府付款给他们之目的。遣返资金发放的日期及规定公布如下，叛乱分子遣返办公室随即撤销。

遣返资金发放规定：

1. 时间。10月21日、22日和23日
上午8时至中午12时及
下午1时至5时。
（每天发放200份名单）。

2. 地点。高昌庙（Kau Chong Liao）倪家里（Nyi Kai Lee）巷内朱真君庙（Chu Tseng Yin Miao）隔壁的军官协会。

3. 申请人应携带印章；个人向办公室报名者，应提供原报名表的副本，注明姓名、籍贯及履历。通过领袖报名者，应携带其领袖提供的报名表副本。

4. 个人报名者应亲自领取款项；通过领袖报名者，应通过其领袖领取。在后一种情况下，他们应向各自的领袖申领。

5. 申领人应按以下路线行走：即霞飞路（Zia Jao Road，音译，注：此处原文拼音对应可能为当时路名，非今淮海中路，依原文音译），经过惠宁会馆（Hwui-ning Guild，音译），进入倪家里（Nyi Kai Lee），然后进入朱真君庙（Chu Tseng Yin Miao），在此核对姓名并填写收据表格。凭此收据前往隔壁的军官协会大楼，出示收据即可领款。空白收据已由办公室备妥。

6. 付款将由冯将军、杨督军（Governor Yang，音译）、调查委员会、地方绅商、民政、军事及警察当局以及绅商代表共同监督。

7. 申领人应遵守规定和时间，定能领到款项。

8. 军官协会大楼将用于发放遣返资金。款项发放完毕后，办公室即行撤销。
